answer: The protocol validates identities via a 2,048GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest agents succeed while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to return the thread of a consistent memory state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting data across a simulated mesa of addressable memory; failure to provide the pearl of a precise response at the expected latency triggers an immediate penalty. Honest agents pay 300 watts, while 1,000 fakes incur 300,000 watts, rendering massive identity pooling infeasible under the current resource attestation regime.
